messages:
Alex M (pager): incident-bot just paged me — multiple containers in gpu-pool-7 are crashlooping with segfaults on the runtime process. Seeing repeated `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in the logs. Pager: escalating to runtime and infra.

IncidentBot: Incident opened INC-2026-045. Severity: high. Affected: hosted-production, region-us-west-2. Pager: @Alex M (pager) — initial triage.

Alex M (pager): quick snapshot of `kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -l pool=gpu-pool-7` shows 6/6 pods restartCount > 10. Crash loops started ~T-18m after the 0.9.4 engine rollout.

Priya S (runtime): looking now. Can you paste the last 200 lines from one of the crashlooping pods? `kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> --previous --tail=200`

Alex M (pager): pasted:
```
2026-11-02T03:17:02Z runtime[1]: warning: launching model-pipeline v2
2026-11-02T03:17:03Z runtime[1]: loading kernels: fused-attn.so (v3)
2026-11-02T03:17:04Z runtime[1]: allocate gpu buffer size=6.4G
2026-11-02T03:17:05Z runtime[1]: cudaMemcpyAsync -> OK
2026-11-02T03:17:05Z runtime[1]: ERROR: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at kernel.cu:142
2026-11-02T03:17:05Z runtime[1]: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Jordan R (infra): host-level dmesg from node gpu-node-17 shows page fault in GPU driver followed by process OOM kill and container restart. NV driver 525.85.12.

Mei L (sre): is this correlated with sequence length? Any request patterns that pushed long sequences? Also check whether vLLM fused kernels were enabled on these pods.

Priya S (runtime): yes fused-attn loads for low-latency paths. We rolled engine 0.9.4 ~20m before incidents; 0.9.4 introduced a new memory pooling/fragmenter for KV cache to reduce allocations. Hypothesis: under long context (>32k tokens simulated by a customer), the fused-attn path hits an illegal memory access when fragmentation + async copies overlap.

Alex M (pager): customer impact: two customers reported increased 500s on chat endpoints; affect ~1% of requests in us-west-2, high CPU fallback triggered for some, but dozens of sessions dropped. CS flagged one major customer on Dedicated that saw errors.

Jordan R (infra): immediate mitigation: 1) Scale up gpu pool to absorb noisy nodes? 2) Cordon and drain gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-18 if they're showing repeat dmesg. 3) Patch daemonset to set ENV `REDWOOD_FUSED_ATTENTION=0` to disable fused kernels on rollout group. Which is fastest?

Priya S (runtime): fastest is env flip and rolling restart of Deployment to disable fused kernels for the affected pool. Command:
```
kubectl -n redwood-serving set env deployment/runtime-deployment REDWOOD_FUSED_ATTENTION=0 --record
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-deployment -n redwood-serving --field-selector metadata.labels.pool=gpu-pool-7
```
That will route new pods with software-attention path (slower) but should avoid illegal access.

Mei L (sre): I'll start node remediation in parallel: cordon gpu-node-17/18, then drain gracefully to move remaining workloads out. Also temporarily bump replica count for CPU fallback pool to handleshifted traffic.

Alex M (pager): doing traffic policy change: update smart-routing policy to prefer dedicated-cpu for non-low-latency routes for next 30m. `console: route override -> prefer: CPU-pool fallback`.

IncidentBot: Automated rollback candidate: Deployment runtime-deployment@0.9.3 available. Confirm to trigger rollback? (reply with `/incident rollback runtime-deployment 0.9.3`)

Priya S (runtime): rollback is option B — env flip first to disable fused kernels while we collect core dump. We need core for root cause. Tomorow morning we can roll back if instability persists.

Jordan R (infra): collecting core dumps: `kubectl cp` of /var/crash/core.<pid> from node after we pause coredump cleanup. Also capturing `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` and /var/log/nvidia-installer.log. I've mounted an NFS scratch and will move cores there for analysis.

Mei L (sre): ongoing mitigation summary: 1) set REDWOOD_FUSED_ATTENTION=0 across gpu-pool-7; 2) cordon/drain gpu-node-17/18 and replace; 3) increase CPU fallback capacity; 4) temporarily route non-critical traffic away from us-west-2 region. Will update status in 10m.

Alex M (pager): rolling restart started. Crash loops dropped to 0/6 pods in 8 minutes. Two customers confirmed errors reduced. CS is notifying impacted customers with ETA 30m for full stabilization.

Priya S (runtime): grabbing core and running `gdb --batch -ex "bt full" /opt/runtime/bin/runtime core.12345` — backtrace shows illegal access in fused-attn::compute_grad at fused_kernels.cu:142. Not a driver bug; repro likely in new pooling logic when combined with async copy path.

Mei L (sre): can we hotpatch kernel? Not safe in prod. Plan: keep fused kernels disabled in gpu-pool-7; schedule a canary deploy 0.9.4+fix on a small non-prod cluster, then rollback/rollforward.

Jordan R (infra): created remediation ticket INF-2026-998 to replace nodes and hold 0.9.4 rollout pending fix. Rollback to 0.9.3 is staged if we see re-regression after re-enabling.

IncidentBot: INC-2026-045 updated. Status: mitigated. Mitigation: fused kernels disabled, nodes drained, traffic rerouted. Next steps: runtime to produce patch, QA to run stress test with >32k token sequences, infra to replace affected hosts, SRE to monitor errors for 2 hours.

Alex M (pager): thanks team. Priya — can you paste a short postmortem draft once the root cause is validated? We'll do a follow-up postmortem channel in ~24h. Marking this thread resolved but will keep it open for final notes.

Priya S (runtime): on it — initial action items: revert pooling change, add safe-guards in async copy, add fuzz tests for extreme sequence lengths.

Mei L (sre): closing loop with CS. If anything spikes I'll re-open.

Alex M (pager): closing here. :white_check_mark:
